input.nl_prompt: Email addresses must be in valid format like name@domain.com

gold._doc_justification:
Email validation in a NetSuite-to-Rootstock migration should typically be a soft check (severity='warning') because legacy customer records often carry non-standard emails (sales-rep notes pasted into the email field, comma-separated email lists, malformed exports from older CRMs). Setting severity='blocking' would halt the migration on every malformed email and force per-record manual fix-up before any data lands in Rootstock — operationally untenable for migrations with >5000 customer records.

The regex is the simplified RFC 5322 form (no comment / quoted-pair / IP-literal support; covers ~99.9% of real-world emails). Case-insensitive because email addresses are case-insensitive in the local-part per RFC 5321 §2.4 (modulo edge cases that don't matter for migration validation).

rule_type='regex' is the canonical mapping for 'must match email format' NL prompts in Settle's existing rule taxonomy (per validation_rules.rule_type CHECK constraint at supabase/migrations/006_data_quality.sql line 14).
_doc_citations: RFC 5322 — Internet Message Format, simplified email production for validation
RFC 5321 §2.4 — Internet Mail Service: case-insensitive local-part

metadata.author: claude
uncertainty_flags: Severity choice: 'warning' (gold) vs 'blocking' is a project-policy decision, not a technical one. Picked 'warning' because that's the operational default for legacy-data migrations; some SOC 2-aligned project policies would mandate 'blocking'. Kaan to confirm Settle's default policy.

Regex strictness: simplified RFC 5322 (gold) vs strict RFC 5322 (rare; covers more edge cases at the cost of complexity) vs 'contains @ and a dot' (loose). Picked simplified as the best practical fit for migration validation; flag if Kaan prefers a different baseline.

field_id encoding: spec proposed an opaque UUID in the example; for the calibration sample this gold uses 'Customer__c.Email__c' (table.field) as a stable cross-environment identifier. The runner translates to the synthetic UUID at eval time.
